title: The Signature Approach to Sub-Nanometer Transistors (Signature)
provenance: Signature original design work by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH). Signature-labeled original designs and improvements — original work, not presented as established public fact.
description: The Signature approach treats the end of shrinking as a design problem: CFET stacking, 2D channels from a real foundry process, backside power, and 3D logic — density keeps climbing after the transistor stops shrinking. This is Signature original work by Justin Addam Higgins: an original design direction for Sub-Nanometer Transistors, labeled as Signature throughout, and never presented as established public fact. Signature angstrom computing ships as chiplet tiles: CFET logic with 2D channels, powered from the backside, stacked in 3D, cooled by microfluidics. Moore's law continues as an integration law.

Signature vision: Signature angstrom computing ships as chiplet tiles: CFET logic with 2D channels, powered from the backside, stacked in 3D, cooled by microfluidics.
Original work: designed by Justin Addam Higgins, Signature-labeled throughout.
